 Spanish Records at risk at the Valencia Half Marathon
 23 October, 2026 
 The Valencia Half Marathon Trinidad Alfonso Zurich is the best stage for setting top marks and breaking records, and the runners themselves confirmed it today at the official elite athletes press conference held at Expo 21K Feria Valencia. 
 Prior to that, Juan Botella , general manager of Sociedad Deportiva Correcaminos, highlighted that “the 21K is in a transition period; the legs that used to dominate the distance have moved to the marathon. Now it’s time for a new generation, and those are the athletes who will run the Valencia Half Marathon. What happens here on Sunday will be a beginning. Remember their names and their faces”. 
 Along the same lines, José Antonio Redolat , selector of the race’s Spanish elite field, confessed that “this is the year with the highest level among national athletes, in both the men’s and women’s categories.” “Every year it gets easier to convince runners to come and race in Valencia,” he added. 
 A very Spanish half marathon 
 Rodri Kwizera , with a time of 58:16, holds the best mark in the entire men’s field competing for victory in Spain’s top half marathon and one of the fastest in the world. “My goal is to run faster. Besides, I really enjoy running in Valencia ,” said Kwizera who, if he achieves a personal best, poses a threat to Carlos Mayo’s Spanish record of 59:39, set in Valencia in 2023. 
 Thierry Ndikumwenayo confessed that in 2024, when he clocked 59:42, he had not done half-marathon-specific training. “This year I have, and on Sunday I’m going to try to improve my time. Rodri will try to go under 58, and in my case, running 58:30 would make me very happy. Competing alongside Kwizera is easier because he is more than a friend, we are like brothers—though once we are in the race, we are neither brothers nor friends,” he admitted. 
 For her part, Carla Gallardo , who is in great form and keeps breaking national records (holding the half marathon record with 1:08:30 and the 10K with 31:11), has done “a very demanding preparation and pushed myself right to the limit this season. The half marathon is a very rewarding distance, and we’ll go all out on Sunday. I know I can run between 1:08 and 1:09. The goal is to lower my personal best.” Meanwhile, Laura Luengo (1:08:50) arrives “with special excitement because I haven’t competed in a long time. So I’m really looking forward to it, and what better place than Valencia. I feel lucky to be here. My goal is to stay with Carla. In fact, having her here is a great opportunity for me. I’ll jump on the bandwagon and hold on with her as long as I can.” 
 Valencia in the Top 10 
 According to international elite selector Marc Roig , “we like to run extremely fast in Valencia. Usually we compete against ourselves; however, we’d like to put Valencia back into the top 10.” That is the intention of South Africa’s Maxime Chaumeton , who holds a 26:55 in the 10K and is making his distance debut. He acknowledged that “ there is no better place to make a debut at this distance. It’s a privilege to be here and I hope to have a good race on Sunday. Moving up in distance was easy because the training is the same—you just have to run double the distance. I’ll give my best to try and reach the podium.” On his end, Tadese Worku (58:35) confessed that he feels good running in Valencia and hopes everything goes well in a city he already knows well, having placed 4th in 2022 and 12th in 2023. 
 On the other hand, Ethiopia’s Tsigie Gebreselama returns to Valencia (1:04:21) after winning in Lisbon in 2025 and 2026. This is her third time in the city of running, and she hopes to “have a good race on Sunday.” Meanwhile, Kenya’s Caroline Gitonga (1:06:16) admitted to feeling more comfortable “with the 10K distance, but I’m getting used to the half marathon.”
